cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is reconstitution of a partnership firm?
cards.back: Any change in the existing agreement amounts to reconstitution of the partnership firm. This results in an end of the existing agreement and a new agreement comes into being with a changed relationship among the members of the partnership firm and/or their composition. However, the firm continues.
cards.quote: Any change in the existing agreement amounts to reconstitution of the partnership firm. This results in an end of the existing agreement and a new agreement comes into being with a changed relationship among the members of the partnership firm and/or their composition. However, the firm continues.

source.section: Introduction

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Name the ways in which partners often resort to reconstitution of a firm.
cards.back:
admission of a new partner
change in profit sharing ratio
retirement of a partner
death or insolvence of a partner
cards.quote: The partners often resort to reconstitution of the firm in various ways such as admission of a new partner, change in profit sharing ratio, retirement of a partner, death or insolvence of a partner.

source.section: Introduction

cards.note: Four modes: admission, change in profit sharing ratio, retirement, and death (or insolvency) of a partner.

sections.title: 2.1 Modes of Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: A new partner may be admitted when the firm needs ____ or ____.
cards.back: A new partner may be admitted when the firm needs additional capital or managerial help.
cards.quote: A new partner may be admitted when the firm needs additional capital or managerial help.

source.section: 2.1 Modes of Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: According to the Partnership Act 1932, a new partner can be admitted into the firm only with the ____ unless otherwise agreed upon.
cards.back: According to the Partnership Act 1932, a new partner can be admitted into the firm only with the consent of all the existing partners unless otherwise agreed upon.
cards.quote: According to the Partnership Act 1932, a new partner can be admitted into the firm only with the consent of all the existing partners unless otherwise agreed upon.
blanks: consent of all the existing partners

source.section: 2.2 Admission of a New Partner

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Name the two main rights a newly admitted partner acquires in the firm.
cards.back:
Right to share the assets of the partnership firm
Right to share the profits of the partnership firm
cards.quote: A newly admitted partner acquires two main rights in the firm— 1. Right to share the assets of the partnership firm; and 2. Right to share the profits of the partnership firm.

source.section: 2.2 Admission of a New Partner

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: For the right to share in the assets and profits of the firm, what does a new partner bring?
cards.back: For the right to acquire share in the assets and profits of the partnership firm, the partner brings an agreed amount of capital either in cash or in kind.
cards.quote: For the right to acquire share in the assets and profits of the partnership firm, the partner brings an agreed amount of capital either in cash or in kind.

source.section: 2.2 Admission of a New Partner

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is the additional amount a new partner contributes on admission known as?
cards.back: the new partner is required to contribute some additional amount known as premium or goodwill.
cards.quote: the new partner is required to contribute some additional amount known as premium or goodwill.

source.section: 2.2 Admission of a New Partner

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Name the 6 important points needing attention when a new partner is admitted.
cards.back:
1. New profit sharing ratio
2. Sacrificing ratio
3. Valuation and adjustment of goodwill
4. Revaluation of assets and Reassessment of liabilities
5. Distribution of accumulated profits (reserves)
6. Adjustment of partners' capitals
cards.quote: Following are the other important points which require attention at the time of admission of a new partner: 1. New profit sharing ratio; 2. Sacrificing ratio; 3. Valuation and adjustment of goodwill; 4. Revaluation of assets and Reassessment of liabilities; 5. Distribution of accumulated profits (reserves); and 6. Adjustment of partners' capitals.

source.section: 2.2 Admission of a New Partner

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: When new partner is admitted he acquires his share in profits from the ____.
cards.back: When new partner is admitted he acquires his share in profits from the old partners.
cards.quote: When new partner is admitted he acquires his share in profits from the old partners.

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On admission of a new partner, what do the old partners do with a share of their profit?
cards.back: In other words, on the admission of a new partner, the old partners sacrifice a share of their profit in favour of the new partner.
cards.quote: In other words, on the admission of a new partner, the old partners sacrifice a share of their profit in favour of the new partner.

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On admission, how are the new partner's share, and how he acquires it from the old partners, decided?
cards.back: what will be the share of new partner and how he will acquire it from the existing partners is decided mutually among the old partners and the new partner.
cards.quote: But, what will be the share of new partner and how he will acquire it from the existing partners is decided mutually among the old partners and the new partner.

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: If nothing is specified, how is the new partner assumed to acquire his share from the old partners?
cards.back: However, if nothing is specified as to how does the new partner acquire his share from the old partners; it may be assumed that he gets it from them in their profit sharing ratio.
cards.quote: However, if nothing is specified as to how does the new partner acquire his share from the old partners; it may be assumed that he gets it from them in their profit sharing ratio.

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On admission of a new partner, what happens to the profit sharing ratio among the old partners?
cards.back: In any case, on admission of a new partner, the profit sharing ratio among the old partners will change keeping in view their respective contribution to the profit sharing ratio of the incoming partner.
cards.quote: In any case, on admission of a new partner, the profit sharing ratio among the old partners will change keeping in view their respective contribution to the profit sharing ratio of the incoming partner.

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Formula: an old partner's new share when the share he surrenders to the new partner is given.
cards.back: Old share − Share Surrendered
cards.quote: Nitu's new share = Old share − Share Surrendered

source.section: 2.3 New Profit Sharing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is the sacrificing ratio?
cards.back: The ratio in which the old partners agree to sacrifice their share of profit in favour of the incoming partner is called sacrificing ratio.
cards.quote: The ratio in which the old partners agree to sacrifice their share of profit in favour of the incoming partner is called sacrificing ratio.

source.section: 2.4 Sacrificing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Formula: the sacrifice by a partner.
cards.back: Old Share of Profit − New Share of Profit
cards.quote: The sacrifice by a partner is equal to : Old Share of Profit − New Share of Profit

source.section: 2.4 Sacrificing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: For the loss of which share must the new partner compensate the old partners?
cards.back: the new partner is required to compensate the old partner's for their loss of share in the super profits of the firm
cards.quote: the new partner is required to compensate the old partner's for their loss of share in the super profits of the firm

source.section: 2.4 Sacrificing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Sacrificing ratio: what three forms could the agreed ratio take?
cards.back:
old ratio
equal sacrifice
a specified ratio
cards.quote: This amount is shared by the existing partners in the ratio in which they forgo their shares in favour of the new partner which is called sacrificing ratio. The ratio is normally clearly given as agreed among the partners which could be the old ratio, equal sacrifice, or a specified ratio.

source.section: 2.4 Sacrificing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: In such a situation, the sacrificing ratio is to be worked out by ____ each partner's ____ from his old share.
cards.back: In such a situation, the sacrificing ratio is to be worked out by deducting each partner's new share from his old share.
cards.quote: In such a situation, the sacrificing ratio is to be worked out by deducting each partner's new share from his old share.

source.section: 2.4 Sacrificing Ratio

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What is the new partner's share of goodwill (premium for goodwill)?
cards.back: As stated earlier, the incoming partner who acquires his share in the profits of the firm from the existing partners brings in additional amount to compensate them for loss of their share in super profits. It is termed as his share of goodwill (also called premium for goodwill).
cards.quote: As stated earlier, the incoming partner who acquires his share in the profits of the firm from the existing partners brings in additional amount to compensate them for loss of their share in super profits. It is termed as his share of goodwill (also called premium for goodwill).

source.section: 2.5.5 Treatment of Goodwill

sections.title: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ____.
cards.back: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice.
cards.quote: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice.

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: new partner brings premium for goodwill in cash through the firm (first entry).
cards.back:
Bank A/c Dr.
To Premium for Goodwill A/c
(Amount brought by new partner as premium)
cards.quote: Bank A/c Dr. To Premium for Goodwill A/c (Amount brought by new partner as premium)

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Alternative entries: premium for goodwill credited to the new partner's capital account and then adjusted to the sacrificing partners.
cards.back:
Bank A/c Dr.
To New Partner's Capital A/c
(Amount brought by new partner for his share of goodwill).
New Partner's Capital A/c Dr.
To Sacrificing Partner's Capital A/c's (Individually)
(Goodwill brought by new partners distributed among the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio)
cards.quote: (i) Bank A/c Dr. To New Partner's Capital A/c (Amount brought by new partner for his share of goodwill). (ii) New Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partner's Capital A/c's (Individually) (Goodwill brought by new partners distributed among the existing partners in their sacrificing ratio)

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Goodwill premium credited to old partners is retained in business: what additional entry is passed?
cards.back: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.
cards.quote: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: existing partners withdraw the goodwill amount credited to them.
cards.back:
Existing Partner's Capital A/c (Individually) Dr.
To Bank A/c
(The amount of goodwill withdrawn by the existing partners)
cards.quote: Existing Partner's Capital A/c (Individually) Dr. To Bank A/c (The amount of goodwill withdrawn by the existing partners)

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

sections.title: When goodwill already exists in books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is ____ at the time of admission of a partner.
cards.back: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.
cards.quote: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.

source.section: When goodwill already exists in books

sections.title: When the new partner does not bring goodwill

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: When the new partner does not bring his share of goodwill, what two possibilities exist?
cards.back:
(a) Goodwill does not exist in the books;
(b) Goodwill exists in the books.
cards.quote: When the new partner does not bring the share of goodwill, there exists two possibilities : (a) Goodwill does not exist in the books; and. (b) Goodwill exists in the books.

source.section: When the new partner does not bring goodwill

sections.title: Goodwill does not exist in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Goodwill does not exist in the books: which partners are credited and which partner is debited?
cards.back: When goodwill does not exist in the books, sacrificing partners are credited with their share of goodwill and new partner is debited by the amount of goodwill not brought by him.
cards.quote: When goodwill does not exist in the books, sacrificing partners are credited with their share of goodwill and new partner is debited by the amount of goodwill not brought by him.

source.section: Goodwill does not exist in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: new partner does not bring his share of goodwill (no goodwill in the books).
cards.back:
Incoming (New) Partners Current A/c Dr.
To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c (individually)
(Account of goodwill not brought in by new partner)
cards.quote: Incoming (New) Partners Current A/c Dr. To Sacrificing Partners Capital A/c (individually) (Account of goodwill not brought in by new partner)

source.section: Goodwill does not exist in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: New partner brings only part of the goodwill premium in cash: which account is debited for the rest?
cards.back: Sometimes the new partner brings part of premium for goodwill in cash. In such a situation, new partners current account will be debited by the amount not brought by new partner.
cards.quote: Sometimes the new partner brings part of premium for goodwill in cash. In such a situation, new partners current account will be debited by the amount not brought by new partner.

source.section: Goodwill does not exist in the books

sections.title: When goodwill exists in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Goodwill appearing in the books will be ____ by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their ____.
cards.back: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.
cards.quote: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.

source.section: When goodwill exists in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Thereafter new value of goodwill will be given effect by crediting ____ and debiting ____.
cards.back: Thereafter new value of goodwill will be given effect by crediting sacrificing partners' capital accounts and debiting new partners' current account.
cards.quote: Thereafter new value of goodwill will be given effect by crediting sacrificing partners' capital accounts and debiting new partners' current account.

source.section: When goodwill exists in the books

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: goodwill appearing in the books is written off when it exists (old partners' capital accounts).
cards.back:
Partners capital A/c (old)
Dr. (In profit sharing ratio)
To Goodwill A/c
(Goodwill appearing in the books written-off)
cards.quote: Partners capital A/c (old) Dr. (In profit sharing ratio) To Goodwill A/c (Goodwill appearing in the books written-off)

source.section: When goodwill exists in the books

sections.title: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: In what forms does a firm usually hold accumulated profits not yet transferred to partners’ capital accounts?
cards.back: Sometimes a firm may have accumulated profits not yet transferred to capital accounts of the partners. These are usually in the form of general reserve, reserve and/or Profit and Loss Account.
cards.quote: Sometimes a firm may have accumulated profits not yet transferred to capital accounts of the partners. These are usually in the form of general reserve, reserve and/or Profit and Loss Account.

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: The new partner is ____ to have any share in such accumulated profits.
cards.back: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits.
cards.quote: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits.

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On admission of a new partner, how are the firm’s accumulated profits distributed?
cards.back: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits. These are distributed among the partners by transferring it to their capital current accounts in old profit sharing ratio.
cards.quote: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits. These are distributed among the partners by transferring it to their capital current accounts in old profit sharing ratio.

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On admission of a partner, how are accumulated losses (debit balance of P&L A/c, deferred revenue expenditure) dealt with?
cards.back: Similarly, if there are some accumulated losses in the form of a debit balance of profit and loss account and/or deferred revenue expenditure appearing in the balance sheet of the firm. It should be transferred to the old partners' capital accounts
cards.quote: Similarly, if there are some accumulated losses in the form of a debit balance of profit and loss account and/or deferred revenue expenditure appearing in the balance sheet of the firm. It should be transferred to the old partners' capital accounts

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Entry (Illustration 22): debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c transferred to old partners' capital accounts.
cards.back:
Rajinder's Capital A/c Dr.
Surender's Capital A/c Dr.
To Profit and Loss A/c
(Debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c transferred to old partners' capital accounts)
cards.quote: Rajinder's Capital A/c Dr. Surender's Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c (Debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c transferred to old partners' capital accounts)

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Entry (Illustration 27): general reserve transferred to the old partners A and B on C's admission.
cards.back:
General Reserve A/c Dr.
To A's Capital A/c
To B's Capital A/c

cards.quote: General Reserve A/c Dr. To A's Capital A/c To B's Capital A/c (Undistributed profit transferred to A and B)

sections.title: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: At admission of a new partner, why are assets revalued and liabilities reassessed?
cards.back: In case the assets are overstated or understated, these are revalued. Similarly, a reassessment of the liabilities is also done so that these are brought in the books at their correct values.
cards.quote: In case the assets are overstated or understated, these are revalued. Similarly, a reassessment of the liabilities is also done so that these are brought in the books at their correct values.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On revaluation, the balance of the Revaluation Account goes to whose capital accounts, and in what ratio?
cards.back: For this purpose the firm has to prepare the Revaluation Account. The gain or loss on revaluation of each asset and liability is transferred to this account and finally its balance is transferred to the capital accounts of the old partners in their old profit sharing ratio.
cards.quote: For this purpose the firm has to prepare the Revaluation Account. The gain or loss on revaluation of each asset and liability is transferred to this account and finally its balance is transferred to the capital accounts of the old partners in their old profit sharing ratio.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: On revaluation, which changes are credited to the Revaluation Account and which are debited?
cards.back: the revaluation account is credited with increase in the value of each asset and decrease in its liabilities because it is a gain and is debited with decrease in the value of assets and increase in its liabilities is debited to revaluation account because it is a loss.
cards.quote: In other words, the revaluation account is credited with increase in the value of each asset and decrease in its liabilities because it is a gain and is debited with decrease in the value of assets and increase in its liabilities is debited to revaluation account because it is a loss.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Similarly unrecorded assets are ____ and unrecorded liabilities are ____ to the revaluation account.
cards.back: Similarly unrecorded assets are credited and unrecorded liabilities are debited to the revaluation account.
cards.quote: Similarly unrecorded assets are credited and unrecorded liabilities are debited to the revaluation account.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: If the revaluation account finally shows a ____ then it indicates net gain and if there is a debit balance then it indicates ____.
cards.back: If the revaluation account finally shows a credit balance then it indicates net gain and if there is a debit balance then it indicates net loss.
cards.quote: If the revaluation account finally shows a credit balance then it indicates net gain and if there is a debit balance then it indicates net loss.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.front: Journal entry: increase in the value of an asset.
cards.back:
Asset A/c Dr.
To Revaluation A/c
(Gain)

cards.front: Journal entry: reduction in the value of an asset.
cards.back:
Revaluation A/c Dr.
To Asset A/c
(Loss)

cards.back:
Revaluation A/c Dr.
To Liability A/c

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry on revaluation of assets and liabilities: reduction in the amount of a liability.
cards.back:
Liability A/c Dr.
To Revaluation A/c
(Gain)
cards.quote: For reduction in the amount of a liability Liability A/c Dr. To Revaluation A/c (Gain)

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry on revaluation of assets and liabilities: an unrecorded asset.
cards.back:
Asset A/c Dr.
To Revaluation A/c
(Gain)
cards.quote: For an unrecorded asset Asset A/c Dr. To Revaluation A/c (Gain)

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry on revaluation of assets and liabilities: an unrecorded liability.
cards.back:
Revaluation A/c Dr.
To Liability A/c
(Loss)
cards.quote: For an unrecorded liability Revaluation A/c Dr. To Liability A/c (Loss)

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: transfer of gain on revaluation (credit balance).
cards.back:
Revaluation A/c Dr.
To Old Partners Capital A/cs
(Old ratio)
(individually)
cards.quote: For transfer of gain on Revaluation if credit balance Revaluation A/c Dr. To Old Partners Capital A/cs (Old ratio) (individually)

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Journal entry: transfer of loss on revaluation (debit balance).
cards.back:
Old partner's Capital A/cs Dr.
(Individually)
(Old ratio)
To Revaluation A/c
cards.quote: For transferring loss on revaluation Old partner's Capital A/cs Dr. (Individually) (Old ratio) To Revaluation A/c

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Entries for a rise or fall in an asset's or a liability's value: what amount is recorded in them?
cards.back: are recorded only with the amount increase and decrease in the value of assets and liabilities.
cards.quote: Note: Entries (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) are recorded only with the amount increase and decrease in the value of assets and liabilities.

source.section: 2.7 Revaluation of Assets and Reassessment of Liabilities

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Sometimes, at the time of admission, the partners agree that their capitals should also be adjusted so as to be ____ to their profit sharing ratio.
cards.back: Sometimes, at the time of admission, the partners agree that their capitals should also be adjusted so as to be proportionate to their profit sharing ratio.
cards.quote: Sometimes, at the time of admission, the partners agree that their capitals should also be adjusted so as to be proportionate to their profit sharing ratio.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: If the new partner's capital is given, how can the new capitals of the old partners be calculated?
cards.back: if the capital of the new partner is given, the same can be used as a base for calculating the new capitals of the old partners.
cards.quote: In such a situation, if the capital of the new partner is given, the same can be used as a base for calculating the new capitals of the old partners.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Adjustment of capitals: what does the partner whose capital falls short do, and the partner with a surplus?
cards.back: The capitals thus ascertained should be compared with their old capitals after all adjustments relating to goodwill reserves and revaluation of assets and liabilities, etc. have been made; and then the partner whose capital falls short, will bring in the necessary amount to cover the shortage and the partner who has a surplus, will withdraw the excess amount of capital.
cards.quote: The capitals thus ascertained should be compared with their old capitals after all adjustments relating to goodwill reserves and revaluation of assets and liabilities, etc. have been made; and then the partner whose capital falls short, will bring in the necessary amount to cover the shortage and the partner who has a surplus, will withdraw the excess amount of capital.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: In such a situation each partner's capital (including the new partner's capital to be brought by him) is calculated on the basis of his ____.
cards.back: In such a situation each partner's capital (including the new partner's capital to be brought by him) is calculated on the basis of his share in profits.
cards.quote: In such a situation each partner's capital (including the new partner's capital to be brought by him) is calculated on the basis of his share in profits.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Subject to agreement, how can surplus or deficiency in old partners' capital accounts be settled?
cards.back: surplus or deficiency in each old partners' capital accounts can also be taken care of simply by transfer to their respective current accounts.
cards.quote: surplus or deficiency in each old partners' capital accounts can also be taken care of simply by transfer to their respective current accounts.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

Cash A/c Dr.

B's Capital A/c Dr.
C's Capital A/c Dr.

source.section: 2.8 Adjustment of Capitals

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Summary: matters needing adjustment in the firm's books when a new partner is admitted.
cards.back:
goodwill
revaluation of assets and liabilities
reserves and other accumulated profits and losses
the capitals of the old partners' (if agreed)
cards.quote: Various matters which need adjustments in the books of firm at the time of admission of a new partner are : goodwill, revaluation of assets and liabilities, reserves and other accumulated profits and losses and the capitals of the old partners' (if agreed).

source.section: Summary
